principle: Facility scale grows only when the need, throughput and strategic role justify fixed infrastructure at that scale.

temporary_support.default_preference: Use before permanent construction when feasible.

micro_outpost.requirement: One narrow sustained function with clear site advantage.
micro_outpost.anti_inflation: No broad resupply/repair/trade services unless separately justified.

small_station.requirement: Several sustained service demands or one high-value specialist function.
small_station.anti_inflation: Must not grow into generic all-services stop.

standard_station.requirement: Sustained regional throughput/population or strong strategic/industrial function.
standard_station.anti_inflation: Services remain bounded by design/capability; not every standard station has shipyard, hospital and diplomacy.

starbase.requirement: Regional-scale military/economic/administrative demand, high traffic, major fleet support or equivalent exceptional strategic value.
starbase.anti_inflation: Rare. Existing starbases strongly suppress generation of another overlapping starbase unless redundancy/war/expansion justifies it.

major_complex.requirement: Exceptional polity-scale industrial, fleet, population or capital-system demand.
major_complex.anti_inflation: Procedural generation disabled by default; require authored/canonical anchor or explicit high-level world-development event.

escalation_rules: A lower-scale facility should be preferred when it can satisfy projected demand with acceptable queue/load.
Expansion is favored over constructing a nearby duplicate when topology/site/sovereignty permits.
Chronic saturation can justify expansion or a second facility only after traffic/service history demonstrates sustained unmet demand.
War may justify temporary or permanent redundancy, but postwar drawdown can mothball/decommission excess capacity.
Population growth alone does not mandate an orbital station if planetary infrastructure already serves the need.
